item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports explicitly separating persistent preference from current intent. [TLSTSRec (2024 online; 2025 issue)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) models temporal duration and spectrum, then adaptively fuses long- and short-term sequences. [IBLSRec (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/) uses inferred intent to refine user preferences while separating stable item relationships from transient relationships. For complementary-item discovery, [Fusing temporal and semantic dependencies (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457324002553) separately learns global/local item transitions and stable semantic dependencies; these capture associations, however, rather than establish functional complementarity. Practical inference for this task: combine a full-history encoder with a recent-window encoder through a learned gate conditioned on observed time gaps and representation disagreement. This is a proposed adaptation, not a demonstrated result on the pinned benchmark.\n\nRepeat-consumption research emphasizes timing and context rather than frequency alone. [TSRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) combines user-specific repeat timing, item-specific intervals, and similarity between current and previous repeat sequences. [MgRIA (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037) models repurchase intervals as mixtures of decay and periodic peaks. [GDA-REIM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026001838) separates repetition/exploration scoring while suppressing shared attention noise through gated differential attention. Transfer constraint: literal repeat-item scoring cannot help the simulator’s unseen-item recommendations directly. Instead, test whether renewed interest in a historical cluster predicts unseen related items, using histories, timestamps, and available titles/descriptions. Treat recurrence as evidence of latent intent; select architectural changes through macro validation HR@10, without assuming simulator traits are observed."}
